actual_scope: Proof note on the block-mask window of the P104 port set: the window w = rank/k of a k-block pattern on the ports (zero blocks on orthogonal pairs, invertible diagonal blocks) is the fractional Haemers bound of the odd graph on the ports (Theorem 1); w >= 53/6 on P104 over every field, w = 9 exactly on P112 and P120 in characteristic 2, w >= 13 on P104 in odd characteristic (Theorems 2 to 4); an exact 14-port pattern of rank 17 at k = 2 and a drat-trim-verified F_2 formula showing no rank-17 pattern at k = 2 on all of P104 (a cross-check of Theorem 3); tensor lift and the column-restriction lemma c_k >= k c_1 for tensor windows (Theorem 5).
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a joint helper basis and a legal causal split on the complete invoice. This package builds no word and prices no supplier. It states and proves structural facts about the port window that any block-window construction on P104 must respect, each with its hypotheses, and keeps what is open at a named question.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the statements bound the window of the port set from below and say what a tensor lift can and cannot give. They say nothing about the denominator or about kappa.
stop_rule: No kappa claim and no new word. Open and stated: the value of w on P104 in characteristic 2 in [53/6, 9] (first undecided block size k = 6, rank 53); whether weights on more ports or other subsets raise 53/6; upper bounds in odd characteristic; a block representation below 9 that is not a tensor lift.
evidence: README.md and THEOREM.md (statements, proofs, hypothesis ledger), check.py and check_sat.py with checks/ (exact integer, rational and finite-field computations, standard library only) and data/ (port list, E8 line map, 14-port representation, recorded solver results, DRAT proof file).

open_questions.question: Is w(P104; F_2) equal to 9, or is it below 9? (Currently 53/6 <= w <= 9.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: A window below 9 is the only way a block-window construction on P104 could beat the one-block value; Theorem 3 excludes every block size k <= 5 and leaves k = 6, rank 53 as the first undecided case.
open_questions.first_step: Decide the existence of a 6-block pattern of rank 53 on P104 over F_2 (Theorem 3 uses 30 ports, so start with the formula on the 30 ports of K and its 22 edge ports, then extend).
open_questions.blocked_by: Not run: the k = 3 formula at rank 27 (about 887,000 variables) was not decided in 20 minutes of kissat, and a k = 6 formula is larger; no representation with ratio in [53/6, 9) is known, so the encoding has not been tested for sharpness.

open_questions.question: Can Theorem 3 be extended to use ports outside K and its edge ports, so that the floor rises from 53/6 to 9?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would settle the question above by hand and show that no block window on P104 beats 9 over any field.
open_questions.first_step: Add the ports with six odd K-neighbours as stand-ins for the six missing edge ports and derive the star and edge inequalities for triangles of mixed ports.
open_questions.blocked_by: Such a port is orthogonal to K only in two coordinates, so its labels live on six K-blocks and the edge inequality becomes much weaker; the star block-diagonality holds only for subfamilies meeting pairwise in one vertex.

open_questions.question: What is w(P104; F) in odd characteristic, between 13 and the one-block value?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only the lower bounds 13, 14, 15 (from the E8 Gram partner) are proved; the upper side is open.
open_questions.first_step: Compute upper bounds from clique covers (fractional chromatic number of the complement) and compare with 13.
open_questions.blocked_by: No upper bound is proved in this package.

open_questions.question: Does a block pattern on P104 with ratio below 9 exist that is not a tensor lift, and what would it cost in a construction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Tensor width f gives rank 9f only (Theorem 5), and a tensor window cannot reduce the per-copy decoder price (c_k >= k c_1), so any gain from a window below 9 needs a new block representation.
open_questions.first_step: Settle the existence question above for k = 6, then price the decoder on the resulting non-tensor window.
open_questions.blocked_by: The first step is open; the decoder price on a non-tensor window is not covered by the column-restriction lemma.
